[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L3 adds oral exposure experiments such as AUC, Cmax, and related PK measurements. Interpret dose, route, formulation, species, sampling, and comparator together; these records inform but do not create extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Verapamil, the most transferable context (dimethoxyphenyl tertiary amine), has absolute oral bioavailability values of 52 ± 13%, 52.3%, 38.17%, and 22% in cirrhosis patients, all at or above the 20% threshold.
Valbenazine, which shares a dimethoxy-substituted fused bicyclic core and basic amine, has absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 49% in humans.

Encainide, a basic methoxy-substituted aryl amide, has mean absolute oral bioavailability of 42 ± 24% (range 7.4–82%) and 41.9%, with a 30 ± 7% record; the mean supports F ≥ 20% despite wide variability.

Noscapine, a polymethoxylated alkaloid, has human oral bioavailability of about 30–31% and mouse F of 26.68 ± 3.8%; the qualitative 'poor' descriptor reflects high-dose requirements, not a sub-20% absolute F.
Sulpiride/levosulpiride, basic methoxy-substituted drugs, show human absolute F of about 24.8–35% (F_AUC 0.248, F_U 0.280; ~27–35%), above threshold; the rat value of 15% is species-limited.

The only clear low record, alfentanil F = 1% (C28), conflicts with other alfentanil records of 37–45% (C03, C25, C31, C45) and is not structurally similar to the query, so it does not support a low prediction.
Additional less similar contexts also report F values above 20%: codeine 40–90%, colchicine 25–55%, and praziquantel 27.2% in cirrhosis, reinforcing the high direction.

L3 oral AUC/Cmax records for verapamil (C49), donepezil (C55), prazosin (C58), and other basic/methoxy-substituted molecules show measurable oral exposure, consistent with oral absorption but not direct F evidence for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
L3 records report oral AUC/Cmax but lack matched IV comparators, so they do not directly quantify absolute F.
Transfer relies on structural analogy; exact first-pass, lactam metabolism, and transporter effects of the query are unknown.
Verapamil cirrhosis records vary (22–52%) and the alfentanil 1% outlier is unresolved.
No formulation, dose, or fed/fasted data are available for the query.
L3 records are non-gold mechanistic context, not independent endpoint measurements.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F ≥ 20%) because the most transferable L1/L2 contexts (verapamil, valbenazine, encainide, noscapine, sulpiride/levosulpiride) consistently show absolute oral bioavailability above 20%; L3 oral AUC/Cmax records for structurally similar molecules are consistent with oral exposure but do not provide direct F evidence, so the prior high prediction is retained without further strengthening.
